punchline: Eleven candidates, and the fifth was the one Kepler married.
thirty_sec: After his first wife died in 1611, Kepler weighed eleven candidates and wrote to a baron about them. He married the orphan Susanna Reuttinger in 1613; the secretary-problem rule for eleven candidates says to skip four, then take the first who beats them all.
question: How many options will you only look at before you let yourself say yes?
key_contrast: First measure the field, then commit to the first option that beats it.
